definition: PATR-II is a linguistic formalism used in computational linguistics, developed by Stuart M.
details: Shieber. It uses context-free grammar rules and feature constraints on these rules.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. And that is PATR-II — teaching a machine to read between the lines.
